roadmap.goal: Save the previewed Release as a Delivery that is identified by the Release rather than by a name someone typed: the binding persists, Jira owns the name, date and Feature list, the aggregate refuses every hand-write to them, and Unbind hands all three back editable.

validation.findings: 3 BLOCKER, 5 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 6 LOW - all closed
validation.root_cause: The roadmap's model of DeliveriesController and Delivery was verified for the CREATE path and ASSUMED for the UPDATE path and the aggregate constructor. Every BLOCKER and four of the five HIGHs sat in phase 02, which is the part that was assumed; phases 01, 03 and 04 were found structurally sound. The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: reading one action of a controller does not tell you the shape of its sibling, and having read an aggregate's methods does not mean you have read its constructor.
blockers: B1 - the future-date guard is in THREE places, not one. Delivery.cs:25-28 throws from the constructor and DeliveriesController.cs:159 calls it, so making only the controller's create guard conditional would send a past-dated Release into an unhandled 500. CLOSED: 01-03 deletes the constructor guard per delta:1042 and updates the two specs that assert it (DeliveryTest.cs:52 and :67); 02-01 and 02-02 make the two controller guards (:138-141 and :183-186) mode-conditional, each carrying a criterion that Manual and RuleBased still reject a past date now that the aggregate no longer does.

B2 - the update step was unbuildable as drafted. UpdateDelivery calls Rename at :216 and Reschedule at :217 BEFORE ApplyFeatureSelection at :219, so once the refusals land every update of a bound Delivery throws at :216 - unbind and repoint both, making AC-02.4 unreachable over HTTP. The Manual arm at :388 also calls SelectFeaturesByHand, which Ruling 2 turned into a refusal. CLOSED: 02-02 now requires the mode transition to resolve BEFORE any name/date/feature mutation, routes unbind through Unbind rather than the Manual arm, and makes :183-186 mode-conditional with an explicit criterion that unbinding a past-dated bound Delivery succeeds.

B3 - the standalone date step was rewritten out of existence rather than amended; see orchestrator_notes.date_step_removed. It was inverted in the DAG, internally contradictory, and had nothing to reduce because ReadReleaseDate already parses to UTC midnight. CLOSED: the server half became two criteria in 02-01, the browser half moved to 03-02, and phase 02 renumbered cleanly to 02-01 / 02-02 / 02-03.
highs: H1 - the browser-day trap was half-owned and the half a user actually sees was owned by nobody. dateInputValue (DeliveryCreateModal.tsx:347-352) builds the field from local getMonth/getDate/getFullYear, and isValidFutureDate (:354, called at :399 and :531) blocks saving a past-dated Release client-side. CLOSED as two criteria in 03-02, with the zone varied per case via an injected formatter or fake timers rather than the globally-pinned runner.
H2 - the display half of B3; closed with it.

H3 - 03-02 silently required widening three SHARED descriptor interfaces: DeliverySelectionPayload (:28-32), DeliverySelectionState (:17-21, where sourceOptionPicked is a BOOLEAN and so cannot tell toPayload which option was picked) and DeliverySelectionValues (:11-15). CLOSED: all three named as criteria, the house shared-contract rule applied, and the descriptor tests required to assert the two built-in tabs are unaffected.

H4 - 03-03 claimed AC-02.2's read-only half and could not prove it in its own files, since DeliverySection.tsx holds no editable control. The real mechanism is readsFromSource at DeliveryCreateModal.tsx:463 driving disabled= at :709 and :723, which would otherwise have shipped as an unasserted side effect - the same defect class that blocked the 01a roadmap. steps.name: Author the slice 01b scenarios together with the contract surface they name
criteria: DeliverySelectionMode gains exactly one member, SourceBound = 2, APPENDED after RuleBased. Manual stays 0 and RuleBased stays 1.

A test pins the numeric value of all three members as literal ints, so a future insertion in the middle fails a test rather than silently repointing every stored Delivery. The enum is persisted as an int with no HasConversion, so the numbers are the storage format.

Delivery gains exactly four properties - SourceKey, SourceReference, SourceLastSyncedOn and SourceUnavailableReason - all nullable and all with NO CLR initializer, following the backing-field idiom at Delivery.cs:12-16 and :48-79 rather than plain auto-properties, because Unbind has to write the first two.

SourceLastSyncedOn and SourceUnavailableReason are deliberately UNWRITTEN in this slice. They ship now so the all-provider migration is paid exactly once; slices 02 and 03 give them behaviour. Their permanent null is by design, not a defect, and no step in this roadmap may start populating them.

Delivery gains BindToSource and Unbind signatures, and all FIVE existing mutators - Rename, Reschedule, ReplaceFeatures, SelectFeaturesByRule and SelectFeaturesByHand - gain a source-bound refusal path. Signatures only at this step; behaviour lands in 01-03.
A DeliverySourceBoundException sibling to DeliveryArchivedException carries a DeliveryId, a stable Code string and static factory methods, matching DeliveryArchivedException.cs exactly.
Every scenario authored in this step is decorated [Ignore] with a scaffold message, so the suite stays green and dotnet build carries zero warnings.

The scenarios cover, at minimum: create-and-bind persists the mode, the handler key and the Version id; the five hand-mutation refusals; Unbind returns the Delivery to Manual retaining name, date and Features.
Every scenario name states the behaviour, not the method under test.
No migration is generated in this step and no endpoint is touched.
dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test green with the live-connector categories excluded.
steps.implementation_notes:
THIS STEP EXISTS BECAUSE DISTILL DELIBERATELY STOPPED SHORT. The maintainer's reasoning, feature-delta.md:1466-1473: in C# an acceptance test cannot reference a type that does not exist without stopping the whole test project compiling, so the scenarios for slices 01b, 02, 03 and 05 land at the head of their own DELIVER slice, in the same commit as the persistence they are about. That is what this step pays off. It is not scope creep and it is not a DISTILL failure.

THE APPEND-ONLY RULE IS THE WHOLE RISK. feature-delta.md:50 (S3) and :782-783: DeliverySelectionMode is int-persisted with no conversion. Inserting a member anywhere but the end silently repoints every stored Delivery to a different mode, with no error and no log line. DDD-4 (delta:949-950) settles the shape: ONE appended member SourceBound = 2 for all handlers, never one per handler, because the handler is a column and the enum must not grow with concepts. The frontend mirror at WorkItemRules.ts:6-9 gains the same number in 03-01; the two are a hand-maintained twin pair, which this repo has been bitten by before.

EXACT SHAPE ON DISK, verified. DeliverySelectionMode.cs is 8 lines holding Manual = 0 and RuleBased = 1. Delivery.cs is 322 lines; :12-16 declares the private backing fields and :48-79 the properties that read them, each under a narrow pragma disabling S2292 with its justification written inline in plain language. That idiom exists precisely because the aggregate's own methods must reach the field while callers may only set it at construction, which is exactly the shape the two new columns need. DeliveryArchivedException.cs is the exception precedent: sealed, extends InvalidOperationException, exposes DeliveryId and Code, static factories returning a kebab-case code plus a sentence. DeliveryArchivedInvariantTest.cs is the refusal-spec precedent; see :77, :88 and :130 for the Assert.Throws idiom and, more importantly, for the discipline of asserting the state the refusal LEFT BEHIND rather than only that it threw.

THE REFUSAL SET IS FIVE, NOT FOUR - MAINTAINER RULING, 2026-08-24. DDD-5 (delta:951-954) names four: Rename, Reschedule, ReplaceFeatures and ApplyRuleSet. On disk the fourth is SelectFeaturesByRule (Delivery.cs:110), not ApplyRuleSet - map the name, do not create a second method. The other three are at :84, :92 and :142. Delivery.cs:100 carries a fifth, SelectFeaturesByHand, which DDD-5 does not mention, and the maintainer has ruled that it refuses too. Bound means Jira owns the Feature list, so a caller who wants to pick by hand calls Unbind first - the documented path, which already retains the last synced name, date and Features. The reason is structural rather than stylistic: permitting it would let someone flip a bound Delivery to Manual without clearing SourceKey, leaving a Delivery that claims Manual while still carrying a handler key. That half-bound state must not be reachable. Write all five refusals as settled scenarios, not as an open question.

STALE LINE IN THE DELTA, do not trust it. feature-delta.md:1248 says these four mutators have zero occurrences today and are ADR-164's to create, and marks sub-slice 01b-ii a hard dependency on that. It was written before #5698 archiving shipped. All four exist now and DeliveryArchivedInvariantTest already exercises two of them. Write the refusals against the methods that are there.

THE PAYLOAD SHAPE IS SETTLED, verified against live code. UpdateDeliveryRequest marks Name, Date and FeatureIds [JsonRequired], and that one DTO binds BOTH create and update - there is no CreateDeliveryRequest. Those attributes STAY. A source-bound payload therefore still sends all three, and the SERVER IGNORES them, taking name, date and membership from the resolved source instead - the only reading consistent with D4 giving the remote ownership of them. Write the scenarios to that contract: a source-bound create carrying a deliberately WRONG name and date must persist Jira's values, not the client's. 02-01 implements it on create and 02-02 on update; the date-storage half is a criterion in 02-01, not a step of its own.

TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): unit specifications are NUnit 4.6 + Moq + EF InMemory on the backend and Vitest + React Testing Library on the frontend. Where a contract is a rule over a range of inputs, express it as an NUnit [TestCase]/[TestCaseSource] family or a Vitest it.each table rather than one hand-picked example, and assert the whole state delta the operation is supposed to produce - including the slots that must NOT change. Integration and E2E remain single-example: they prove wiring, not invariants. Here that means the five refusals are ONE [TestCaseSource] family over the mutators, each case asserting both the throw and that name, date, Features, mode, handler key and source reference are all unchanged.

CI LEDGER, pre-applied: NUnit2056 - never Assert.Multiple with a lambda, always using (Assert.EnterMultipleScope()). NUnit2045 judges the METHOD, so a shared private assertion helper needs its own scope. CA1861 - hoist any inline new[] passed to an assertion into a private static readonly field; ten recurrences on record and the pre-commit hook has been seen to miss it three times. CA1869 - if any new test file touches JSON, cache JsonSerializerOptions in a static readonly field. Commit: test(deliveries), one focused commit.

steps.name: Expand-only migration for both providers
criteria: The four [NotMapped] attributes 01-01 put on SourceKey, SourceReference, SourceLastSyncedOn and SourceUnavailableReason are REMOVED in this same commit. 01-01 could not ship them mapped - a mapped column with no migration turns EF PendingModelChangesWarning into a throw on every migrating boot, which reds 174 tests across key custody, telemetry, startup and the Testcontainers Postgres fixtures. The attributes and the migration must appear and disappear together; splitting them across two commits leaves one of the two states broken.

SourceUnavailableReason takes its real CLR type, DeliverySourceUnavailableReason?, replacing the int? 01-01 used as a placeholder. The enum already exists at Models/DeliverySources/DeliverySourceUnavailableReason.cs from slice 01a. EF maps an int-backed enum as an int column, so this is storage-identical and costs no second migration - but it must happen HERE, before the migration is generated, or the generated column carries the wrong CLR type in the snapshot.
The migration is generated by running Lighthouse.Backend/Create-Migration.ps1 with a MigrationName, never by invoking dotnet ef migrations add directly.

Both providers land in the same commit: Lighthouse.Migrations.Sqlite/Migrations/ and Lighthouse.Migrations.Postgres/Migrations/. A commit carrying one and not the other is a broken commit, because the script generates them as a pair and only the pair describes the schema.

The migration is expand-only: it adds four nullable columns - SourceKey, SourceReference, SourceLastSyncedOn and SourceUnavailableReason - and does nothing else. No DropColumn, no AlterColumn, no rename, no data backfill.
All four ship in THIS migration even though only the first two are written in this slice, so the Docker-backed two-provider generation is paid exactly once. MAINTAINER RULING, 2026-08-24.
The generated Up method is read by hand and contains only AddColumn calls. If it contains anything else the model changed more than intended - stop and report rather than editing the generated file.
Both LighthouseAppContextModelSnapshot.cs files are regenerated and committed alongside the migrations.
An existing Delivery row with all four columns null loads and behaves byte-identically to before this slice, so an instance that never binds anything is unaffected.

A round-trip spec proves a bound Delivery keeps its mode, SourceKey and SourceReference across a save and reload, and that SourceLastSyncedOn and SourceUnavailableReason are STILL NULL afterwards - the forward columns are unwritten by design in this slice.

If the four properties use the backing-field idiom, LighthouseAppContext configures field access for them the way it already does for the Features collection at :445; if convention already resolves the backing field, no configuration is added and the round-trip spec is what proves it.
dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test green with the live-connector categories excluded.
steps.implementation_notes:
BUILD THE BACKEND BEFORE YOU RUN THE SCRIPT. Lighthouse.Backend/Migrations/ holds only the two built DLLs, Lighthouse.Migrations.Sqlite.dll and Lighthouse.Migrations.Postgres.dll, referenced by HintPath. dotnet ef reads the ModelSnapshot compiled INTO those DLLs, so a stale or absent build makes the tooling report pending model changes that are not real - and the natural response, regenerating until it agrees, produces a wrong migration. The slice brief calls this out under Watch, and docs/ci-learnings.md:1053 records it costing a cycle: after checkout churn an incremental build left a stale DLL and dotnet ef reported pending against an out-of-date snapshot even though the .cs was correct. Build first, every time.

THE SENTINEL TRAP, and why 01-01 forbade CLR initializers. Same ledger entry, first half: a model property written as public bool HasSufficientData { get; set; } = true; makes EF treat true as the property SENTINEL, because the initializer differs from the type default, and the model-differ then never reconciles cleanly - perpetual pending. The sibling column FilterApplied has no initializer and works. All four new columns are nullable, and a nullable's type default is null; give them no initializer and the trap cannot fire. If you add one to silence a nullable-reference warning, you are reintroducing it.

WHAT THE SCRIPT DOES, verified. Create-Migration.ps1 is 83 lines at Lighthouse.Backend/Create-Migration.ps1. It sets Database__Provider=sqlite against a temp .db and runs dotnet ef migrations add --project Lighthouse.Migrations.Sqlite --startup-project Lighthouse.Backend --context LighthouseAppContext (:39-40); then starts postgres:17.2-alpine in Docker as lighthouse-postgres-migration on 5432, switches Database__Provider=postgres, and repeats against Lighthouse.Migrations.Postgres (:56-57); the finally block tears the container down and deletes the temp db. DOCKER MUST BE RUNNING - if it is not, the Postgres half fails AFTER the SQLite half has already written files, leaving exactly the half-generated state the pairing criterion forbids. Check Docker before you start. There is no SQL Server project; two providers is the whole set. Newest migration on both sides today is DropUnusedForecastHowMany (20260822121242 sqlite, 20260822121253 postgres), so the new pair sorts after those.

WHERE THE ENTITY IS CONFIGURED: Data/LighthouseAppContext.cs - DbSet at :45, concurrency token at :266, Portfolio FK at :434, the Features many-to-many at :440 and its field access mode at :445. Four nullable scalar columns need no new fluent configuration beyond field access if the backing-field idiom requires it; if you find yourself adding more than that, ask why. If SourceUnavailableReason is modelled as a nullable enum it persists as a nullable int - keep it a plain scalar with no converter, because slices 02 and 03 own its vocabulary and a converter added now is one a later slice has to unpick.

EXPAND-ONLY IS A RELEASE CONTRACT, not a preference: migrations are additive-only per release, never Recreate, because a released instance upgrades in place.

SCOPE, SETTLED: this migration carries FOUR columns. The maintainer ruled on 2026-08-24 that slice 01b lands SourceKey, SourceReference, SourceLastSyncedOn and SourceUnavailableReason together, matching feature-delta.md:1042 and :1247, which said four all along. The last two stay unwritten until slices 02 and 03. The reason to ship them now is that this script is not a cheap thing to re-run: it wants Docker up, it generates two providers, and adding two nullable scalars later would mean a second full round for no behaviour. That is what the brief means when it names the all-provider migration as 01b's fixed cost. The no-write guard is codified, not left to memory: this step carries it as a criterion, 01-03 asserts both columns are still null after BindToSource and after Unbind, and 02-02 states they serialise as null on the read DTO by design.

TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): unit specifications are NUnit 4.6 + Moq + EF InMemory on the backend and Vitest + React Testing Library on the frontend. Where a contract is a rule over a range of inputs, express it as an NUnit [TestCase]/[TestCaseSource] family or a Vitest it.each table rather than one hand-picked example, and assert the whole state delta the operation is supposed to produce - including the slots that must NOT change. Integration and E2E remain single-example: they prove wiring, not invariants. Here: a [TestCaseSource] over all three selection modes - Manual and RuleBased with all four columns null, SourceBound with SourceKey and SourceReference populated and the two forward columns still null - asserting every persisted slot on the way back, so a mode that loses a column on reload fails rather than passing on the one case someone thought to write.

Commit: feat(deliveries), one focused commit carrying both providers.

CARRIED FROM 01-01, AND THIS STEP IS WHERE IT IS PAID OFF. 01-01 shipped the four properties [NotMapped] and typed SourceUnavailableReason as int?. Both were bridges, not decisions. It measured the alternative: mapping the columns without a migration reds 174 tests spanning key custody, telemetry, startup and the Testcontainers Postgres fixtures - a spread that looks exactly like the known load-contention signature and is not one. Baseline for comparison: unmodified main under the same filter is Failed 0, Passed 5959. If you generate the migration and the round-trip spec still sees nulls, the first thing to check is whether all four attributes actually came off.

steps.name: The aggregate binds, unbinds, and refuses hand-writes while bound
criteria: The [Ignore] attributes authored in 01-01 come off and every scenario passes.

BindToSource sets the mode to SourceBound and records SourceKey and SourceReference, calling MarkAsChanged exactly once so the concurrency token is bumped once. It does not touch SourceLastSyncedOn or SourceUnavailableReason.
Unbind sets the mode back to Manual, clears SourceKey and SourceReference, and LEAVES name, date and Features exactly as they were, so the last synced values survive and become editable again.

SourceLastSyncedOn and SourceUnavailableReason are never written by this step - they ship in 01-02's migration for slices 02 and 03. A spec asserts both are still null after BindToSource and after Unbind, so the forward columns cannot be quietly co-opted.

All FIVE mutators - Rename, Reschedule, ReplaceFeatures, SelectFeaturesByRule and SelectFeaturesByHand - throw DeliverySourceBoundException while the Delivery is source-bound, and each leaves every field unchanged, including the one it was asked to write.

SelectFeaturesByHand is refused rather than treated as an implicit unbind, so no Delivery can claim Manual while still carrying a SourceKey. Unbind is the only route back, and a spec proves that half-bound state is unreachable.
The refusal is distinguishable from the archived refusal: a different exception type and a different Code, so a caller can tell why it was refused.
The archived refusal still fires and still takes precedence where both apply; DeliveryArchivedInvariantTest passes untouched.
The same five mutators behave exactly as before on a Manual or RuleBased Delivery - the refusal is conditional on the mode, not unconditional.
After Unbind, all five mutators are accepted again, proving the refusal is a property of the binding rather than a one-way latch.

THE CONSTRUCTOR'S FUTURE-DATE GUARD IS DELETED. Delivery.cs:25-28 throws ArgumentException with the message about the date having to be in the future, and DeliveriesController.cs:159 calls that constructor - so a past-dated Release would bind straight into an unhandled 500 if only the controller guard were made conditional. delta:1042 already ruled this check deleted; do it here, in the step that owns Delivery.cs.

Deleting it reds the two specs that assert it - DeliveryTest.cs:52 and :67 - which are updated or removed in this same commit with the reason stated. Nothing else in the backend asserts that message from the aggregate.

Date validation does not disappear, it moves: the controller keeps rejecting a past date for Manual and RuleBased at DeliveriesController.cs:138-141 and :183-186, which 02-01 and 02-02 make mode-conditional. A criterion in each of those steps proves the two free-tier modes still refuse a past date once the aggregate no longer does it for them.
No endpoint, DTO or frontend file is touched by this step.
dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test green with the live-connector categories excluded.
steps.implementation_notes:
THIS IS D4 MADE STRUCTURAL. feature-delta.md:132-144: for a source-bound Delivery the work tracking system is the single source of truth for the date AND the membership, and Lighthouse never edits either. DDD-5 (delta:951-954) is explicit that this becomes a property of the AGGREGATE rather than a UI convention - the point being that a direct API call must be refused even though the UI would never make it. Read-only rendering in phase 03 is presentation of this rule, never a substitute for it.

FOLLOW THE ARCHIVED REFUSAL EXACTLY. Delivery.cs:180 is RefuseWhenArchived, a private guard the mutators call, and :196 is MarkAsChanged, which bumps the concurrency token. Write the source-bound refusal as a sibling private guard called from the same five methods, and reuse MarkAsChanged rather than touching the token by hand. Two guards in the same shape are readable; two guards in different shapes are how the precedence question gets answered differently in each method.

UNBIND RETAINS, IT DOES NOT CLEAR. AC-02.4 (delta:388-389) and AC-04.3 (delta:444): unbinding returns the Delivery to Manual with its last synced name, date and Features retained and editable. The easy wrong implementation clears the fields along with the binding, throwing away exactly the data the user unbound in order to keep. Assert the retention explicitly - it is the half of Unbind with no natural failure signal.

WHAT THIS STEP DOES NOT BUILD. ApplySourceSnapshot (DDD-6, delta:955-957) is the sync path's atomic mutator and belongs to slice 02. The record it would take, DeliverySourceSnapshot(Name, Date, MemberReferenceIds), already exists in Models/DeliverySources/ from 01a - leave it alone. Create-time resolution CONSTRUCTS a Delivery rather than mutating one (delta:1247-1248), so the create path in 02-02 needs none of these mutators, which is precisely why the refusals can be this strict without blocking create.

THE FIFTH MUTATOR REFUSES - MAINTAINER RULING, 2026-08-24, settled and not open. SelectFeaturesByHand (Delivery.cs:100) is not an implicit unbind and must not become one. Bound means Jira owns the Feature list, so a caller who wants to pick by hand calls Unbind first - the documented path, which already retains the last synced name, date and Features, so nothing is lost by making them take it. Permitting it would let someone flip a bound Delivery to Manual without clearing SourceKey, leaving a Delivery that claims Manual while still carrying a handler key: an unrepresentable-by-intent state that is very representable in code. Make it unreachable and write the spec that proves it, rather than trusting the guard by inspection.

PRECEDENT TO MIRROR: DeliveryArchivedInvariantTest.cs:70-88 shows the two-assertion shape this codebase uses for a refusal - one spec that it throws, one that it leaves the prior state intact. Copy that discipline; a refusal spec asserting only the throw passes against an implementation that throws AFTER mutating.

TEST PARADIGM (mandatory): unit specifications are NUnit 4.6 + Moq + EF InMemory on the backend and Vitest + React Testing Library on the frontend. Where a contract is a rule over a range of inputs, express it as an NUnit [TestCase]/[TestCaseSource] family or a Vitest it.each table rather than one hand-picked example, and assert the whole state delta the operation is supposed to produce - including the slots that must NOT change. Integration and E2E remain single-example: they prove wiring, not invariants. Here the refusals are one [TestCaseSource] over the five mutators crossed with the three selection modes: fifteen cases where five throw and ten do not, each asserting the full field set. That crossing is what catches an unconditional refusal, which a five-case table covering only the bound mode would happily pass.

CI LEDGER: NUnit2056, NUnit2045, CA1861 as in 01-01. Commit: feat(deliveries).

steps.scenario_name: Creating a Delivery from a Release persists Jira's name, date and Features and ignores whatever the client sent
criteria: POST api/v1/deliveries/portfolio/{portfolioId:int} accepts selectionMode SourceBound carrying a sourceKey and a sourceReference, and persists all three.

PREMIUM GATE, create side. VerifyDeliveryRequest (DeliveriesController.cs:424-449) branches on RuleBased at :426 and lets everything else fall through to the free-tier arm, which returns 403 'Free users can only have 1 delivery per portfolio' at :444 only once a portfolio already has one. A SourceBound create must require CanUsePremiumFeatures outright, so a free-tier user binding their FIRST Delivery from Jira gets 403 rather than a silent allowance.

The switch in ApplyFeatureSelection at DeliveriesController.cs:363-372 gains a SourceBound arm. Without it the new member falls to the default arm and every source-bound create returns 400 while every aggregate unit test still passes.

The server IGNORES Name, Date and FeatureIds on a source-bound create and takes all three from the resolved snapshot. No comparison, no refusal-on-difference. A spec posts a deliberately WRONG name and date and asserts Jira's values are what persist.

The stored date is the snapshot's DateTime verbatim, with NO time-zone reduction and no ILighthouseClock involvement. The date is already UTC midnight by the time the resolver hands it over; reducing it again in a named zone is what would CREATE an off-by-one, not fix one.

A pure spec on JiraReleaseVersionReader.ReadReleaseDate (:68-82) pins that a Jira bare date parses to UTC midnight, via the existing DateTimeStyles.AssumeUniversal | DateTimeStyles.AdjustToUniversal at :77-78, and that an absent releaseDate key yields null rather than a parse failure.
A sourceReference that does not resolve is NOT persisted, and the response distinguishes NotFound from Unavailable so a network blip is never reported as a deleted Release.

The create-side future-date guard at DeliveriesController.cs:138-141 becomes conditional on the mode: a source-bound create skips it, so a Release dated last quarter binds. Manual and RuleBased creates still reject a past date at the controller, and DeliveriesControllerTest.cs:186 and :324 still pass unchanged.
DeliveryWithLikelihoodDto gains the four nullable source fields beside SelectionMode at :50, and FromDelivery maps them; the two forward columns serialise as null by design.

Adding an IDeliverySourceResolver dependency to the primary constructor at DeliveriesController.cs:20 updates all three test construction sites: DeliveriesControllerUtcTest.cs:49-58, DeliveriesControllerTest.cs:335 and DeliveriesControllerArchiveTest.cs:322. All three compile and pass.
Manual and RuleBased create payloads are byte-identical to before this Epic - same fields, same validation, same responses. AC-02.3.
dotnet build zero warnings; dotnet test green with the live-connector categories excluded.

BindToSource and Unbind refuse an ARCHIVED Delivery, calling RefuseWhenArchived the way the five hand-write mutators already do. 01-03 shipped them without that guard - no criterion asked for it and it stayed minimal rather than shipping an untested one - so an archived Delivery can currently be bound or unbound, mutating a frozen aggregate. This step is where the resolution path first calls BindToSource for real, so this is where the guard earns a spec.
TestToday.AFutureDate carries a docstring saying the date is one the Delivery constructors own guard will accept. That guard is gone. Correct the sentence while this step is in the neighbourhood.
steps.implementation_notes:
THIS STEP ABSORBED THE OLD 02-01 DATE STEP, and the reason matters because the old step would have BUILT the bug it claimed to prevent. The draft asked for a zone-parametrised reduction of the Release date, citing LighthouseClockTest.cs:48-50 as precedent. That table exists to prove the calendar day DIFFERS by zone - it is the opposite of the property the step asserted. And there is nothing to reduce: JiraReleaseVersionReader.ReadReleaseDate already parses Jira's bare date with AssumeUniversal | AdjustToUniversal (:77-78), so the server only ever sees UTC midnight and never a browser rendering. Running that through ILighthouseClock.ToInstanceDay would introduce an off-by-one rather than remove one. orchestrator_notes.date_step_removed: An earlier revision carried a step 02-01 whose whole job was to settle a time-zone reduction for the Release date. orchestrator_notes.ignore_not_compare_ruling: MAINTAINER RULING, 2026-08-24. When a Delivery is source-bound the server IGNORES Name, Date and FeatureIds, on create and on update, and takes all three from the resolved snapshot. There is deliberately NO comparison and NO refusal-on-difference. An earlier draft of 02-02 said an update attempting to change those fields is REFUSED, which would have required comparing the client's value against Jira's - and the client's date is a browser-local rendering of a UTC instant that can legitimately arrive a day off, so a comparison rule would have rejected honest saves. THE FIVE HAND-MUTATION REFUSALS ARE UNAFFECTED: they are aggregate-level and still throw, which is what 02-03 proves at the HTTP boundary.
